scope_review: Read the original two production functions, complete materialized floating/discrete kernel families, both public proof files and conversion-gap documentation. Existing partial contracts and full signed-loop semantics are preserved.

All eight public contracts are selected per-program execution/equivalence or mathematical IO; none supplies the complete original wrapper grid and all independently supplied source/destination dtype combinations.

structural_gaps.finding: Original wrapper forwards independently typed source and destination tensors without same-dtype assertion. Kernels.Storage enumerates six floating types (36 pairs), while DiscreteSource.kernel only has nine homogeneous discrete pairs. Mixed floating/discrete and heterogeneous discrete store conversions are outside these public families; source supports no restriction to that union.

Wrapper launches len(old_a_start) programs with BLOCK_SIZE=256. Existing public contracts quantify a single s.pids 0 and its metadata; they do not establish the entire host launch, per-program output collision policy, cross-program aliasing and ordering.

int32/int64 metadata labels both erase to mathematical Int, and other metadata dtypes are not modeled. Loaded starts and loop arithmetic have no established native finite-width overflow/byte-address mapping. This is a representation/dispatch gap, not an arithmetic callback to defer.

Original mask is lane<length rather than i+lane<length. Existing full-loop proofs correctly retain overcopy and require bounds for Math.copiedLength. The wrapper adds no corresponding check. Original host/error domain and safe allocation/collision preconditions still need explicit whole-program coverage; the requested segment length alone cannot justify source safety.

numerical_boundary: A future exact floating-conversion rule may be deferred only after the missing dtype execution route is represented; it cannot discharge an absent source branch, wrapper or finite-address representation.

verification.basis: Read-only scope review against exact source and declaration hashes; no new execution/proof result claimed.
